The document is a standard 9-page Constitution PDF containing the following main points: • Legislative Power: The U.S. Constitution vests all legislative powers in Congress, consisting of a Senate and House of Representatives. • Senate Composition & Voting: Senators are chosen by state legislatures for six-year terms with one vote each; the Vice President presides but has no voting power unless equally divided. No person can be elected to either House without attaining age 25 or being a citizen residing in that State for seven years. • Bill Presentation & Reconsideration: Bills must be presented to the President before becoming law, and if rejected, they are returned with objections from their originating house. After two-thirds of each house agrees to pass a bill, it is sent back for reconsideration; only then does it become law unless the President returns it within ten days. • Concurrence Required: Orders, resolutions, and votes requiring Senate and House concurrence must be approved by the President before taking effect.
